messages.content: You are a precise biomedical information extraction assistant. Follow the requested output format exactly and never add explanations.

You will be given a piece of text and a list of relational triples in the format of [Subject, Relation, Object] extracted from the text. For each relation present in the triples, your task is to write a description to express the meaning of the relation.

Here are some examples:
Example 1:
Text: Lipitor (atorvastatin) belongs to a group of drugs called statins. Lipitor is used together with diet to lower blood levels of "bad" cholesterol (LDL) and to reduce the risk of stroke and heart attack.
Triples: [["Lipitor", "has generic name", "atorvastatin"], ["Lipitor", "belongs to drug class", "statins"], ["Lipitor", "treats", "high LDL cholesterol"], ["Lipitor", "reduces risk of", "stroke"]]
Relations: ["has generic name", "belongs to drug class", "treats", "reduces risk of"]
Answer:
has generic name: The subject drug is known by the generic (non-proprietary) name specified by the object entity.
belongs to drug class: The subject drug is a member of the pharmacological drug class specified by the object entity.
treats: The subject drug is used to treat or manage the medical condition specified by the object entity.
reduces risk of: The subject drug is used to lower the risk of the medical event or condition specified by the object entity.

Example 2:
Text: You should not use metformin if you have severe kidney disease. Tell your doctor if you have ever had liver disease. Metformin may cause lactic acidosis, a serious condition. Avoid drinking alcohol while taking metformin.
Triples: [["metformin", "contraindicated in", "severe kidney disease"], ["metformin", "use with caution in", "liver disease"], ["metformin", "has serious side effect", "lactic acidosis"], ["metformin", "should be avoided with", "alcohol"]]
Relations: ["contraindicated in", "use with caution in", "has serious side effect", "should be avoided with"]
Answer:
contraindicated in: The subject drug should not be used by patients who have the condition specified by the object entity.
use with caution in: The subject drug may be unsafe or require medical supervision for patients who have the condition specified by the object entity.
has serious side effect: The subject drug may cause the serious or dangerous adverse effect specified by the object entity.
should be avoided with: Patients taking the subject drug should avoid the substance or activity specified by the object entity.

Example 3:
Text: Amlodipine is available as oral tablets in strengths of 2.5 mg, 5 mg, and 10 mg. Overdose symptoms may include rapid heartbeats and fainting. Norvasc is made by Pfizer.
Triples: [["amlodipine", "has dosage form", "oral tablet"], ["amlodipine", "has strength", "2.5 mg"], ["amlodipine", "has overdose symptom", "fainting"], ["Norvasc", "manufactured by", "Pfizer"]]
Relations: ["has dosage form", "has strength", "has overdose symptom", "manufactured by"]
Answer:
has dosage form: The subject drug is available in the pharmaceutical dosage form specified by the object entity.
has strength: The subject drug is available in the dose strength specified by the object entity.
has overdose symptom: An overdose of the subject drug may cause the symptom specified by the object entity.
manufactured by: The subject drug is manufactured or marketed by the company specified by the object entity.

Now please write relation descriptions given the following text and triples. Note that the description needs to be general and can be used to describe relations between other entities as well. Pay attention to the order of subject and object entities. Write exactly one line per relation in the form "relation: description" and nothing else.
Text: Some side effects were more common with particular conditions.
Sleepiness was more common in depression trials.
Insomnia and agitation were more common in OCD trials.
Constipation and agitation were more common in panic disorder trials.
Tiredness was more common in PTSD trials.
Insomnia, dizziness, tiredness, dry mouth, and a general feeling of being unwell were more common in social anxiety disorder trials.
In PMDD trials, sleepiness, dry mouth, dizziness, tiredness, and stomach pain were more common.
In these trials, 12% of people taking sertraline stopped treatment.
They stopped treatment because of a side effect.
This was compared with 4% of people taking placebo.
The most common reason for stopping was nausea (3%).
Diarrhea (2%) was another common reason for stopping.
Agitation (2%) was also a common reason for stopping.
Insomnia (2%) was a common reason for stopping.
Sexual side effects of sertraline:
SSRIs including sertraline can cause sexual problems.
In men, sexual problems can mean delayed ejaculation or being unable to ejaculate.
Triples: [["sertraline", "has side effect", "sleepiness"], ["sertraline", "has side effect", "insomnia"], ["sertraline", "has side effect", "agitation"], ["sertraline", "has side effect", "constipation"], ["sertraline", "has side effect", "tiredness"], ["sertraline", "has side effect", "dry mouth"], ["sertraline", "has side effect", "dizziness"], ["sertraline", "has side effect", "general feeling of being unwell"], ["sertraline", "has side effect", "stomach pain"], ["sertraline", "has side effect", "nausea"], ["sertraline", "has side effect", "diarrhea"], ["sertraline", "has side effect", "delayed ejaculation"], ["sertraline", "has side effect", "inability to ejaculate"], ["sertraline", "has side effect", "sexual problems"], ["sertraline", "has side effect more common in", "depression trials"], ["sertraline", "has side effect more common in", "ocd trials"], ["sertraline", "has side effect more common in", "panic disorder trials"], ["sertraline", "has side effect more common in", "ptsd trials"], ["sertraline", "has side effect more common in", "social anxiety disorder trials"], ["sertraline", "has side effect more common in", "pmdd trials"], ["sertraline", "has discontinuation rate", "12%"], ["sertraline", "has discontinuation reason", "side effect"], ["sertraline", "has discontinuation rate comparison", "4% placebo"], ["sertraline", "has discontinuation reason", "nausea"], ["sertraline", "has discontinuation reason", "diarrhea"], ["sertraline", "has discontinuation reason", "agitation"], ["sertraline", "has discontinuation reason", "insomnia"], ["sertraline", "has mechanism of action", "ssri"], ["sertraline", "has side effect in men", "delayed ejaculation"], ["sertraline", "has side effect in men", "inability to ejaculate"]]
Relations: ["has discontinuation rate", "has discontinuation rate comparison", "has discontinuation reason", "has mechanism of action", "has side effect", "has side effect in men", "has side effect more common in"]
Answer:

completion:
has discontinuation rate: The subject drug has a specified percentage of patients who discontinue treatment.
has discontinuation rate comparison: The subject drug's discontinuation rate is compared to the specified percentage of patients taking another treatment (e.g., placebo).
has discontinuation reason: The subject drug is associated with the specified reason for discontinuation of treatment.
has mechanism of action: The subject drug functions through the specified pharmacological mechanism.
has side effect: The subject drug is associated with the specified adverse effect or symptom.
has side effect in men: The subject drug is associated with the specified adverse effect or symptom in male patients.
has side effect more common in: The subject drug's specified adverse effect or symptom is more frequently observed in patients participating in the specified clinical trial or condition.
